Browse recent entries when you have no search word. An agent can use it to see what the journal holds before it adds more.

## MCP tool: list_entries

Deprecated: use find_entries (same filters and more). This tool will be removed in the next minor release. List journal entries, newest first. The text result is JSON. Pass a low `limit` so that the result does not flood your context.

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description | Default |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|---------|
| `project` | `string` | no | Only entries of this project. |  |
| `tags` | `string[]` | no | Only entries that have all of these tags. |  |
| `from` | `string` | no | Only entries from this date (inclusive). Use a local day (YYYY-MM-DD) or an ISO timestamp. |  |
| `to` | `string` | no | Only entries up to this date (inclusive). Use a local day (YYYY-MM-DD) or an ISO timestamp. |  |
| `limit` | `integer` | no | Most entries to return. The newest come first. The maximum is 500. | `50` |

### Output

This tool returns structured output. The shape is the [Entry list](/docs/reference/output-shapes/#entry-list).

## Examples

### MCP

List the two newest entries of one project. Pass a low `limit` so that the result stays short.

```json
{
  "project": "worker",
  "limit": 2
}
```

The structured result. The text result holds the `entries` list as JSON.
